full_judgment:
14. Now, whether the said payment of consideration money is directory or mandatory and whether the consideration money is payable after the statutory period of limitation. For a lawful interpretation of the said requirement of law we profitably laid on our hands section 96 of the State Tenancy Act, 1950 which provides the provisions for filing a pre-emption case against transfer of land by one of the co-sharers tenant of the holding or by contiguous land holder against any stranger purchaser and section 96(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 which provides for making deposit of the consideration money of the transferred land in the Court at the time of filing the case, which runs as under: 

 "96(3)(a) An application made under subsection (1) shall be dismissed unless the applicant or applicants, at the time of making it, deposit in the Court the amount of the consideration money or the value of the transferred holding or portion or share of the holding as stated in the notice under section 89 or in the deed of transfer, as the case may be, together with compensation at the rate of ten per centum of such amount." 

 15. On reading of section 96(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act it shows that the requirement of depositing the consideration money plus compensation at the time of filing of the case has been made mandatory. 

 16. It has been held by our Appellate Division in the case of (i) Md Golam Rabbani vs Habibulla reported in 31 DLR (AD) 87 and in the case of Karimun Nessa Begum vs Niranjan Chowdhury reported in 43 DLR (AD) 108 that the entire consideration money together with the required compensation must be in deposit when the pre-emption application is filed. In the 31 DLR (AD) 108 it has been held that the direction for depositing the balance consideration money being a condition precedent to the application being entertained, its non compliance renders the application liable to be dismissed. The language of section 96(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the language of section 21A of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 are similar and the consequence for non-depositing the contractual amount at the time of filing the suit is fatal rendering the suit to be dismissed. 

 19. In the case of Abdus Sattar ,vs IFIC Bank Ltd. 5 MLR (AD) 83 = 52 DLR (AD) 122 it has been held that the provisions for depositing the money was a condition precedent for preferring the appeal before the High Court Division. Upon consideration of the provisions of section 96(3)(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, section 41 (ii) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 20003 and the decision as discussed above read with section, 21A(b) of the Specific Relief Act we are of the view that the requirement of depositing the balance contractual amount out of the total consideration money at the time of filing the suit for specific performance of contract is mandatory failing which no suit is maintainable and the plaint is liable to be rejected under Or VII, rule 11 (d) of the Code of Civil Procedure.
